[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

All packages follow strict semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.REVISION`) in lockstep across all languages. Releases use a structured notes template. Deprecated APIs remain for at least two MINOR cycles before removal.

---
page_texts.5:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#context-and-problem-statement]

## Context and Problem Statement

- **Business Context**: Multiple teams depend on this framework. They need to know whether upgrading is safe, what changed, and when deprecated APIs will be removed.
- **Technical Context**: All supported languages release in lockstep. Versioning, communication, and deprecation must be consistent.
- **Problem Statement**: What does each version level mean, how are releases communicated, and how long do deprecated APIs live?

---
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#1-semantic-versioning]

## 1. Semantic Versioning

| Level | Meaning | Consumer Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **MAJOR** (`X.0.0`) | Breaking change — interfaces removed, renamed, or changed incompatibly | Consumers MUST update their code |
| **MINOR** (`0.X.0`) | New capability — new interfaces, adapters, or features added | Existing code works unchanged |
| **REVISION** (`0.0.X`) | Fix — bug fixes, performance improvements, doc corrections | No code changes required |
page_texts.7:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#version-lockstep]

### Version Lockstep

All language packages share the same version number at all times. A fix in one language triggers a release for all. This eliminates "which version of which language" confusion.
page_texts.8:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#pre-release-tags]

### Pre-release Tags

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X.Y.Z-alpha.N` | Experimental — interfaces may change |
| `X.Y.Z-beta.N` | Feature-complete — interfaces frozen, bugs expected |
| `X.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — production-ready pending validation |
page_texts.9:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#pre-release-version-format-by-ecosystem]

### Pre-release Version Format by Ecosystem

Each package ecosystem has its own version format rules. The semantic meaning is identical across all languages — only the string representation differs due to registry constraints.

| Language | Format | Example | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C# (NuGet) | `X.Y.Z-rc.N` | `1.0.0-rc1` | SemVer 2.0 |
| Java (Maven) | `X.Y.Z-rc.N` | `1.0.0-rc1` | Maven versioning |
| Python (PyPI) | `X.Y.ZrcN` | `1.0.0rc1` | PEP 440 (hyphens not permitted) |
| Rust (Cargo) | `X.Y.Z-rc.N` | `1.0.0-rc1` | SemVer 2.0 |

This is an inherent ecosystem constraint, not a configuration choice. PyPI normalizes `1.0.0-rc1` to `1.0.0rc1` automatically during upload. All polyglot frameworks (AWS SDK, gRPC, etc.) exhibit this same behavior.
page_texts.10:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#feature-parity-mandate]

### Feature Parity Mandate

All supported languages must maintain **feature parity at all times**. A feature, fix, or enhancement must be implemented in every language before a release is tagged. No language may ship capabilities that others lack.

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **All languages release together** | A fix in one language triggers a release for all — no partial releases |
| **Feature parity required** | Every interface, method, adapter, and behavior exists in every language |
| **BDD contracts enforce parity** | No language passes quality gate unless all shared `.feature` scenarios pass |
| **Language-specific exception** | A change may touch only one language **only** when it addresses a language-specific defect or performance optimization that does not affect the public interface or behavioral contract |

Language-specific exceptions must be documented in the Per-Language Notes section of the release notes and must not alter the interface surface or observable behavior.
page_texts.11:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#what-constitutes-a-breaking-change-major]

### What Constitutes a Breaking Change (MAJOR)

- Removing or renaming a public interface/method
- Changing method signature or documented behavior contract
- Removing or renaming a package
- Forcing consumers to update their dependency tree

page_texts.12:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#2-release-notes-template]

## 2. Release Notes Template

Every release uses this mandatory structure. Sections with no content display "None." — never omitted.

```markdown
# Release vX.Y.Z

**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Type:** MAJOR | MINOR | REVISION
**Previous Version:** vX.Y.Z

---

## Summary
[1-3 sentences — purpose and impact]

## Breaking Changes
| Change | Affected Interface | Migration Required |
| --- | --- | --- |

## New Capabilities
- [Capability — brief description]

## Fixes
- [Fix — what was wrong and what was corrected]

## Deprecations
| Deprecated | Replacement | Removal Target |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Per-Language Notes
### [Language Name]
- [Language-specific changes or "No language-specific changes."]

## Upgrade Instructions
1. Update dependency version to X.Y.Z
2. [Additional steps if needed]

## Migration Guide
[MAJOR only — before/after code examples]

## Dependencies
| Dependency | Action | Old Version | New Version | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Known Issues
- [Issue — description and workaround]

## Contributors
- [Name/team — contribution]
```
page_texts.13:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#template-rules]

### Template Rules

- All sections mandatory — use "None." when empty
- Breaking Changes always first after Summary
- Per-Language Notes always present for each supported language
- Migration Guide uses before/after code examples
- CI validates section presence before release publish

page_texts.14:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#3-deprecation-policy]

## 3. Deprecation Policy

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Active: API introduced
    Active --> Deprecated: Marked deprecated in vX.Y.0
    Deprecated --> Deprecated: Remains in vX.Y+1.0 and vX.Y+2.0
    Deprecated --> Removed: Removed in vX+1.0.0 (next MAJOR)
    Removed --> [*]
```

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Minimum window** | Two MINOR releases must ship after deprecation before removal |
| **Compiler warnings** | Deprecated items emit warnings in all supported languages |
| **Replacement required** | No API deprecated without a documented replacement |
| **Removal only in MAJOR** | Deprecated items removed only in MAJOR bumps |
| **Migration guide** | MAJOR release notes include before/after examples |

---
page_texts.15:
[standards/application/STD-APP-LIB-001-polyglot-library-versioning-and-lifecycle.md#implementation]

## Implementation

- Version declared in `.project.yml` — single source of truth
- CI reads version and applies to all language packages during build
- Git tags use `vMAJOR.MINOR.REVISION`
- Release notes stored in `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md` and on GitHub Release page
